properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-1 is spec-mandated by RFC 4880/4880bis for OpenPGP v4 fingerprints and the legacy SEIP-MDC integrity packet; a library that must interoperate with existing v4 keys cannot remove it. First-party and changeable here only by dropping legacy v4 support; new v6 material already uses SHA2/SHA3 fingerprints.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Test-only keygen: used to check RSA private-key packet parsing with small, fast keys. Not production key material, but it is real 1024-bit RSA key generation in the shipped test binary — kept in the inventory for completeness.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RSA in this OpenPGP library serves both key transport (session-key encryption to RSA keys, PKCS#1 v1.5 as mandated by RFC 4880 §5.1 — production decrypt path in encrypted_key.go covered by the PKCS#1 v1.5 object) and signing (rsa.VerifyPKCS1v15 at public_key.go:1038, SignPKCS1v15 in the sign path). Keygen takes `bits` from caller config (tests use 2048; default RSA keygen in this library is 2048). First-party and changeable here; new keys can be ML-KEM-768/ML-DSA-65, but RSA must stay for existi

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 is implemented for OpenPGP interoperability (some implementations use bitcoin-style keys), but the default policy REJECTS it: the packet/config.go:32 hit is inside defaultRejectCurves, and the library also defaults to rejecting ElGamal/DSA keys and MD5/RIPEMD160/SHA1 message hashes. So the curve ships but is off unless a caller overrides RejectCurves. Classical EC, Shor-broken; changeable here by deleting the bitcurves package.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Test-only weak PRNG: generates random plaintext lengths, headers, nonces, tag sizes and tampering offsets for AEAD property tests (eax/eax_test.go, ocb/ocb_test.go) and random test inputs elsewhere. No production randomness flows through math/rand — the library's runtime randomness is crypto/rand (covered by the CSPRNG object, e.g. rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, ...)). Kept as a true observation of a weak PRNG in the tree; its C rating overstates production risk.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 is the library's OpenPGP ECDH implementation (Curve25519 secret/public point handling in internal/ecc/curve25519.go), used to encrypt session keys to v4 X25519 subkeys — a "harvest now, decrypt later" path. It is also the classical component of the shipped PQ hybrids (ML-KEM-768+X25519 composite, benchmark_v6_test.go:62). Quantum-vulnerable (Shor); changeable here by preferring the ML-KEM-768 hybrid the library already implements, though X25519 must stay for legacy v4 key interoperability

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 is the library's OpenPGP EdDSA signature implementation — openpgp/ed25519/ed25519.go is a wrapper over cloudflare/circl's ed25519 (OpenPGP's Ed25519 uses a distinct point encoding, hence the custom Sign/Verify/keygen wrapper). Production sign/verify path for v4 Ed25519 keys, and the classical half of the ML-DSA-65+Ed25519 hybrid. Quantum-vulnerable (Shor); migrate signatures to ML-DSA-65 — the library already ships both standalone ML-DSA and the hybrid.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The library's full ECDSA support for OpenPGP keys: keygen (key_generation.go:308 via ecc.FindECDSAByGenName; internal/ecc/generic.go:79), signing (packet/signature.go:1024 ecdsa.Sign; generic.go:125), verification (public_key.go:1056 ecdsa.Verify; generic.go:130), key parse/serialize (openpgp/ecdsa package; private_key.go:157/875/1031-1043), and tests over NIST P-256 and brainpool curves. properties.value: X448 key agreement as an OpenPGP encryption-subkey primitive (PubKeyAlgoX448, RFC 9580): circl dh/x448 KeyGen/Shared primitives (internal/ecc/x448.go:9-100), keygen dispatch (key_generation.go:393), PKESK wrap with HKDF-SHA512 (x448.go:146, confirmed under ALG-ab44ea08), Ed448_X448 benchmarks and RFC 9580 test vectors. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed448 is the library's OpenPGP Ed448 signature wrapper over cloudflare/circl (Sign/Verify/GenerateKey/NewKeyFromSeed in openpgp/ed448/ed448.go), production path for Ed448 v6 keys and the classical half of the ML-DSA-87+Ed448 hybrid. 224-bit classical security but Shor-broken like all EC; migration target ML-DSA-87, already shipped as the hybrid.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: This object's sites conflate two curve families, both genuine classical EC: (a) the Brainpool curves brainpoolP384r1/t1 and brainpoolP512r1/t1 implemented in brainpool/brainpool.go for EU/German OpenPGP interoperability (~192/256-bit classical security), and (b) NIST P-384/P-521 handling in the library's ecc layer. All are Shor-broken; B rating reflects interim CNSA strength, not quantum safety. Changeable here only by dropping legacy curve support; new keys should use the ML-KEM hybrids.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Production post-quantum KEM: the mlkem_ecdh package implements the OpenPGP ML-KEM+ECDH hybrid key types. Both parameter sets ship — ML-KEM-768+X25519 (v4-style allowed, v6 preferred) and ML-KEM-1024+X448 (v6-only, enforced at key_generation.go:401). FIPS 203; this is migration-target posture for key agreement, not a weakness. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Production post-quantum signatures: the mldsa_eddsa package implements the OpenPGP ML-DSA+EdDSA hybrid signature key types — ML-DSA-65+Ed25519 and ML-DSA-87+Ed448 (v6-only, enforced at key_generation.go:327), dispatched in clearsign at clearsign.go:539. FIPS 204; migration-target posture for signing. Both 65 and 87 parameter sets recorded. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) signature support for v6 OpenPGP keys: parameter sets SLH-DSA-SHAKE-128s/128f/256s registered as public-key algorithm IDs 32-34 (packet.go:528-530), v6-only key generation (key_generation.go:345-350 via packet.GetSlhdsaSchemeFromAlgID), private-key parse/serialize/validate (private_key.go:573/893-947/1277-1287), and integration tests. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-3 (SHA3-256/SHA3-512) is a supported OpenPGP hash algorithm per the crypto-refresh: registered with OpenPGP hash IDs 12/14 in internal/algorithm/hash.go:40-41, dispatched in clearsign signing (:529,531) and hash preference handling, used by v6 keys. Grover-resistant with 256/512-bit output; A- only because CNSA 2.0 prefers SHA-384/512. Target-state hash, no migration needed. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-128 is a supported OpenPGP symmetric cipher (algorithm ID 7) in internal/algorithm/cipher.go, and newly generated keys advertise it in PreferredSymmetric for interoperability (key_generation.go:121-122 appends CipherAES128 when the configured cipher differs). Used with CFB (legacy v4) and AEAD modes. Quantum-resistant (block cipher), A- only because Grover halves it to 64-bit and CNSA 2.0 prefers AES-256. Changeable here (could prefer AES-256 only), but interop with older peers keeps AES128

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Every site in this object names the SLH-DSA-SHAKE signature parameter sets — SLH-DSA-Shake-128s/128f/256s, OpenPGP algorithm IDs 32-34 (packet.go:528-530) — whose internal hash is SHAKE128/SHAKE256. SHAKE is not invoked as a standalone XOF on these sites; the substance is the SLH-DSA (SPHINCS+) post-quantum hash-based signature family, recorded under the SLH-DSA entry. Merged so a reader references one entry instead of chasing the same SLH-DSA sites under two names.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES block cipher at the base of every OpenPGP symmetric path: the cipher registry (internal/algorithm/cipher.go:91 — AES-128/192/256, wire IDs 7/8/9; default message cipher is AES-128 per packet/config.go), the RFC 3394 AES Key Wrap used for v5/v6 PKESK and ECDH wrap (openpgp/aes/keywrap/keywrap.go:59/:108), EAX/OCB AEAD tests (eax/eax_test.go, ocb/ocb_test.go — key sizes 16/24/32) and legacy OCFB tests (packet/ocfb_test.go). Quantum-safe symmetric primitive (Grover: AES-128 keeps a 64-bit quant

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Argon2id is the RFC 9580 S2K KDF for v6 symmetric-key-encrypted packets: production argon2.IDKey at s2k/s2k.go:178 with packet-driven parameters (passes/memory/parallelism validated at :423-432; parallelism=0, iterations=0 rejected), backed by golang.org/x/crypto/argon2. Tests use the RFC-recommended t=3, p=4, m=2^16 KiB. Memory-hard password KDF — target-state, quantum-irrelevant; the relevant question is parameter floors, which follow the RFC.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HKDF (RFC 5869) is the v6/crypto-refresh key derivation throughout: HKDF-SHA256 derives AEAD message keys from the session key (symmetrically_encrypted_aead.go:161), SKE v6 keys (symmetric_key_encrypted.go:328), v6 private-key protection (private_key.go:1207), and the X25519 ECDH wrap key (x25519.go:140); HKDF-SHA512 for the X448 wrap (x448.go:146). go.mod declares the golang.org/x/crypto/hkdf dependency. Modern, HMAC-based KDF — keep.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 use: v6 key fingerprints (public_key.go:369) and the hash inside every HKDF-SHA256 derivation for v6 AEAD/ECDH/private-key protection. Standard modern hash; no weakness. (Two further sites of the object were already judged.)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Provider-level record: go.mod pins golang.org/x/crypto v0.41.0, whose sha3 sub-package provides the SHA-3 family used for SHA3-256/SHA3-512 hashing in clearsign and signatures, and underlies the SHAKE-based SLH-DSA parameter sets. Usage sites are recorded under ALG-052c24b2 (SHA-3); the dependency pin is what makes them available.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Provider-level record: SHAKE128 (from x/crypto/sha3, pinned v0.41.0 in go.mod) is the underlying XOF for the SLH-DSA-SHAKE-128s/128f parameter sets (algorithm IDs 32/33, see ALG-64af9e41). Usage sites recorded under ALG-6d9e0af5 (SHAKE).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The library's AEAD registry (openpgp/internal/algorithm/aead.go): RFC 9580 AEAD modes EAX, OCB and GCM over AES; cipher.NewGCM at :61 constructs the GCM instance (AEAD mode ID 3). Authenticated encryption used for v5/v6 SEIPD; quantum-safe. The EAX/OCB constructions themselves are recorded under ALG-e4916d9f (CTR/CBC-MAC components in eax.go) and ALG-36a15216 (tag verification).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: CNSA-2.0-compliant digest strength; also the hash inside the X448 public-key KDF. No migration needed — this is the target state for hashes in this library.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Post-quantum hybrid key agreement (ML-KEM-768 combined with classical curves) — this is the migration target posture, not a weakness. Committed test key material in a first-party crypto library; test-only exposure, changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-256 is the preferred OpenPGP cipher in this library (DefaultCipher in v6 tests; algorithm ID 9 in internal/algorithm/cipher.go:34), used for message encryption in CFB and AEAD modes, and as the AES key size in the ECDH key-wrap KDF (KDF{Cipher: AES256} at key_generation.go:383, ecdh_test.go:50,144). Grover leaves a 128-bit margin; CNSA 2.0-compliant symmetric choice. Target state, no migration needed.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Provider-level record: SHAKE256 (x/crypto/sha3, pinned v0.41.0) underlies the SLH-DSA-SHAKE-256s parameter set (algorithm ID 34, see ALG-64af9e41). Usage sites recorded under ALG-6d9e0af5 (SHAKE) / ALG-cfa4b055 sites in go.mod.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto/rand (rand.Reader) is the library's randomness source throughout: key generation (rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader,...), mlkem_ecdh/mldsa_eddsa GenerateKey take config.Random()), ElGamal keygen/encryption in openpgp/elgamal/elgamal.go, session keys, and every algorithm test. This is a positive-posture asset (the secure baseline the weak-PRNG object should be compared against), not a weakness — the ? rating reflects that the collector couldn't grade a non-weakness. No action needed.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Armored PGP MESSAGE blocks embedded in the RFC 9580 interop test-vector suite (integration_tests/testdata/test_vectors.json ×12, v2 copy ×12, test_data/aead-ocb-asym-message.asc): real encrypted-message artifacts, test-only, mostly encrypted under modern AEAD modes; they exercise the library's decrypt paths. No production secrets.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Armored PGP PRIVATE KEY blocks committed as test fixtures: the RFC 9580 interop test-vector keys (test_vectors.json ×24) and the OCB asymmetric test key (test_data/aead-ocb-asym-key.asc, pairs with aead-ocb-asym-message.asc). These are published test-vector keys by design — committed "secret" material with no production value, used to exercise private-key parsing and decryption. Real key artifacts; keep recorded, flagged test-only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Cloudflare circl is the linked post-quantum provider: circl/kem plus mlkem768 and mlkem1024 parameter sets are imported in packet/public_key.go:37-39 and mlkem_ecdh/mlkem_ecdh.go:15. This is what gives the library its ML-KEM (FIPS 203) capability for the ML-KEM+ECDH hybrid key exchange of OpenPGP v6. The provider version (go.mod) decides PQ capability — see LIB-31082111.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Armored PGP SIGNATURE blocks (ASCII-armored detached signatures) embedded as test fixtures in the armor round-trip and signature-parsing tests. Real signature artifacts, test-only, over test data — they exercise armor decode and signature packet parsing. No live key material.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared crypto dependency: golang.org/x/crypto v0.41.0 (go.mod). Supplies hkdf (v6 KDFs — ALG-ab44ea08), sha3 (SHA-3/SHAKE — ALG-c9ef78a4/ALG-d0f975d5/ALG-cfa4b055), argon2 (Argon2id S2K — LIB-16475ac8), and the legacy ripemd160 used only via a test blank-import (s2k_test.go). properties.name: pqs:context

The library IS the algorithm surface being inventoried: it decides which OpenPGP algorithms exist for every downstream application that imports it.
